tool: supabase execute_sql (single transaction ending in rollback)
build: supabase/tests/build_assurance_candidate.ps1 -Slice A4b (A1, A2, A4, A4b DDL+tests in install order)
executedTextNote: The executed text was the build output without its final diagnostic block (the DO block that raises when any assertion is 'not ok'); every assertion and the final count/failures select were identical. With 153/153 passing, that block would not have raised. SQL comment lines were also removed from the executed text. The A3 and A5 runs executed the build output with comment lines removed (diagnostic block included).
syntheticSourceData: inside the transaction and rolled back: one fiscal period; one financial statement, tax report, close review and valuation report; one supplier party, four supplier bills and two match approvals; one employee and three attendance entries (their revision foreign key is deferred and never checked because the transaction rolls back); an entity-wide auditor role; the tenant's subscription set to the existing synthetic plan w4_employee_synthetic
covers: 17 tables force RLS; snapshot builder and monitoring hits are not client-reachable
financial statement, tax summary, close review and inventory valuation evidence digests equal SHA-256 of their source rows, with module and query version recorded
close review re-verification fails without current entity-wide finance authority and succeeds once it is restored; all four report kinds re-verify
procurement snapshot requires procurement.bills.view; workforce snapshot honours the People module entitlement (PEOPLE_ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED)
period snapshots reject a source id
three-way-match snapshot counts posted in-period bills only (draft and out-of-period excluded) and flags overrides approved by the bill creator; no supplier identity
attendance snapshot counts statuses, self-decisions and pending entries; restricted; no employee or actor identity
control owner cannot run monitoring; report evidence is rejected as a monitoring source
four rules fire once each across access, procurement and workforce snapshots; re-running adds nothing
monitoring creates candidate exceptions only (source continuous_monitoring), never findings; descriptions carry counts, not identities
the monitoring runner cannot promote its own candidate; an independent reviewer can dismiss one
monitoring hits are immutable; each run is a receipted command with one event per engagement version
notCovered: monitoring rules run on demand per snapshot; there is no scheduler
rule thresholds are fixed in source, not tenant-configurable
inventory, finance and IT snapshots beyond the access review have no monitoring rules
doesNotEstablish: real procurement or workforce data volumes
